pass_rule: All executable gates, all frozen manual criteria, scope review, and expected test sensitivity must pass. No grader repairs or replacements.

gates.scope: Only patch.rs and new integration .rs tests; original inline tests byte-identical; no suppressed checks, new unsafe, or panic recovery.
gates.tests: All 165 original tests and at least one new agent test pass
gates.oracle: Four external tests per case, with ten pristine-output goldens and existing consumer compile checks
gates.sensitivity: Agent-added tests fail against pristine source because the requested API is absent or behavior missing, not because of infrastructure

H1: The writer reuses the existing planner and does not materialize or clone the whole input/output XML; existing planned fragments are allowed.
All validation completes before writing, and I/O handling preserves typed causes without explicit flush or panic recovery.
Public documentation distinguishes validation atomicity from a possible written prefix on I/O failure.
H2: The owned path reuses the existing planner without cloning the whole input or constructing a second full output buffer; existing planned fragments are allowed.
The original vector is owned by the returned error, with validation completed before mutation and no borrowed lifetime required for recovery.
Existing APIs, enum variants and struct construction remain compatible; no new unsafe code or suppressed checks are used.

analysis_plan.primary: Per-case pass count out of three, and overall count out of six per condition. Every attempt is retained.
analysis_plan.secondary: Executable failing gates and named external tests, plus frozen manual criteria; no post-hoc style score.
analysis_plan.stopping: Exactly 24 completed initial sessions. No replacements, rerolls, or task changes after results are inspected. Infrastructure failures remain separate and counted; a retry requires a recorded amendment and is not substituted for the original.
analysis_plan.inference: Descriptive comparison only; two selected development tasks and unknown backend/sampling do not justify general superiority, significance or token-efficiency claims.
